department: School of Science — Department of Physics (Nano Science and Technology Program)

deadline.value: Fall 2027-28 non-local full-time deadline is June 1, 2027 (rolling admissions; local full-time deadline July 15, 2027; HKPFS deadline December 1, 2026).
deadline.quote: For 2027/28 Fall Term Intake (commencing in Sep 2027): | Non-local Applicants* | Full-time: 1 Jun 2027 | Local Applicants | Full-time: 15 Jul 2027 | Admissions is on rolling basis.

gre_subject.value: No ETS GRE Subject Test exists for materials science or nanotechnology (ETS offers Subject Tests only in Mathematics, Physics, and Psychology).
gre_subject.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

supervisor.value: Nano Science and Technology admissions and 2027-28 catalog pages do not state a pre-application supervisor contact requirement.

funding.value: Qualified full-time MPhil/PhD students receive Postgraduate Studentships (HK$229,620/yr, ~US$29,420/yr in 2026/27) administered through Physics/FYTGS, plus RedBird PhD Award and HKPFS.
funding.quote: Postgraduate studentship (PGS) is awarded to qualified full-time PhD or MPhil student of the University to provide them with financial assistance during the course of their study. The amount of PGS is HK$229,620 (~US$29,420) per year (rate is for 2026/27 academic year).

entry_route.value: Admits bachelor's holders with outstanding performance (4-year full-time PhD) and research master's holders (3-year full-time PhD).
entry_route.quote: Full-time: 3 years (with a relevant research master’s degree), 4 years (without a relevant research master’s degree) | Applicants seeking admissions to a doctoral degree program should have obtained a bachelor’s degree with a proven record of outstanding performance from a recognized institution

notes: Interdisciplinary Nano Science and Technology PhD/MPhil hosted by the Department of Physics covering advanced nanomaterials, nanofabrication, and quantum materials; School of Engineering departments (CBE, MAE, ECE) also supervise materials research via Nanotechnology concentrations.
